clue.text: Maria might be taken in by this view

definitions.text: Maria might be taken in by this view

parts.words: Maria might be taken in by this view
parts.note: Maria is not a woman but the plural of mare, the dark lunar 'seas'; a vista of the Moon's surface would take them in

explanation.surface: A woman named Maria might be fooled, or charmed, by a particular sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria reads as a girl's name; it is really the Latin plural of mare, the name astronomers give the dark plains on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunar landscape, as seen from orbit or the surface, includes the dark plains called seas.

clue.text: Prophet born of the union of Amos and Esther

indicators.note: the two names are joined into one run with the link 'and' dropped, and the offspring is a stretch from the middle of that run

parts.note: the two biblical names written together with nothing between them

explanation.surface: A prophet is said to be the child of a marriage between two Old Testament figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Write AMOS and ESTHER as one 'united' string, AMOSESTHER; the prophet is born from its middle, losing the A at the front and THER at the back. It works like a hidden word across the joined names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament leader who brought the Ten Commandments down from Sinai is counted a prophet.

clue.text: Very few rulers lash corgis, mostly barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters that follow go wild and are rearranged
mostly means most but not all of the word corgis, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A small ruling class beats the royal dogs, which are yapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts CORGIS to CORGI; 'barking' then shuffles LASH plus CORGI. Corgis are the Queen's famous dogs, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an oligarchy, government by a small group, are by definition a handful of people in power.

clue.text: Plant stalk strangling damaged, hard leaf — bother!

indicators.note: strangling means wrapping tightly around, so the stalk word goes round the rest

parts.note: a stalk of a plant is its stem

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the following words have their letters rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gardener's stalk throttles a ruined leaf, and the gardener swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bother' is not an exclamation here but part of the letters 'damaged' rearranges, with H for hard; 'strangling' wraps the stalk round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulbous plant with white starry flowers carries this name, after the guiding light of the Nativity story.

clue.text: Observed announcement, a signal to stop hiding high explosive

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so the explosive sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public announcement
a red light is the signal to stop

explanation.surface: A notice and a stop sign are concealing a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observed' is meant in the sense of observing a rule, sticking to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stuck to the rules kept to them faithfully, past tense in both cases.

clue.text: Chap overwhelmed by mounting support for decoration?

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped, surrounded, so the man's name goes inside the other piece
mounting means climbing, and in a down clue that reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
Paul is simply a man's name, so any chap

explanation.surface: A man is buried under a rising support while getting a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounting' reads upwards; Chap stands for any man's name. The question mark marks the definition as an example: the shoulder piece is ornamental.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform is a kind of military trimming.

clue.text: Tuft of hair slightly altered by a draught

indicators.note: altered by means changed using the following word, so one letter is swapped for it

parts.note: a quiff is a tuft of hair brushed up over the forehead

explanation.surface: Someone's hairdo has been slightly ruffled by a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly altered by a' swaps the I of QUIFF for A. 'draught' is a drink, not a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty swallow of drink, as a noun, is a deep gulp.

clue.text: Dock hosting a recent rent free anniversary

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so the dock word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a quay is a dock or wharf for ships

indicators.note: free means loose, released, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dockside lets a newly leased property go rent free to mark an anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent free' looks like a tenancy term; 'free' is the anagram signal working on the three words before it, and 'hosting' wraps the dock round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-hundredth anniversary is the celebration of four centuries.

clue.text: Girl stops in the morning, by sailor's side?

indicators.note: stops in means plugs a gap inside, so the girl's name goes into the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
Bea is a girl's name, short for Beatrice

explanation.surface: A girl calls in during the morning, sitting beside a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a nautical term: at right angles to the ship's length, level with the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafaring term for at right angles to a vessel's keel, roughly opposite her midship beam.

clue.text: They should cause buzzers to malfunction

definitions.text: They should cause buzzers to malfunction

parts.words: They should cause buzzers to malfunction
parts.note: the buzzers are not doorbells or alarms but flies and wasps, and the products aimed at them should stop them working

explanation.surface: Something is designed to make doorbells or alarms break down.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzzers suggests electrical devices; here they are insects, and the aerosols knock them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerosol insecticides are aimed at flies, the buzzing insects, to kill or disable them.

clue.text: Food inducing trip accompanied by endless pain

parts.note: a spin is a short trip, as in a spin in the car

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the pain word drops its last letter

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Some food brings on a jaunt accompanied by constant pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ACHE to ACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The leafy green vegetable is something eaten, a food.

clue.text: School year's ending after bill made reforms

indicators.note: after places the year's last letter behind the other pieces

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters of made are reshaped
ending means the final letter of the word year's

explanation.surface: A school reorganises at the end of the year once legislation is passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' turns MADE into ADEM; 'ending' takes Y from year's. 'bill' looks parliamentary but is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a place of learning, and in Britain a type of state-funded secondary.

clue.text: Pretty well unnerve old soldier under this

indicators.note: pretty well means almost, so the word for unnerve is not quite complete and loses its last letter

parts.note: to shake someone is to unnerve them

explanation.surface: Something might seriously rattle a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty well' cuts SHAKE to SHAK. The definition is cryptic: a soldier stands under this tall military hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cylindrical peaked cap with a plume is worn on a soldier's head.

clue.text: Plan possibly used at Mafeking?

parts.note: a plan is a map; the siege of Mafeking in the Boer War ended with its famous relief in 1900, so the map would be the one used for that rescue

explanation.surface: A strategy might have been adopted during the siege of Mafeking.
explanation.walkthrough: The siege of Mafeking (1899-1900), in the Boer War, is remembered in Britain for its relief; the solver must combine that word with a plan, a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing hills and valleys by shading or modelling is a contoured chart.

clue.text: Lying here is invalid

parts.note: read as 'this is where the invalid lies', with invalid as a noun for a sick person, not 'lying is not valid'

explanation.surface: A statement that telling lies on this occasion is not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Invalid reads as the adjective, not valid; it is the noun, a patient, and lying means reclining, not fibbing.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed of a patient laid up through illness is where they rest.

clue.text: More than one pro needing small clubs plays for the best of three

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

parts.words: plays for the best of three
parts.note: a rubber, in bridge or tennis, is a series decided by the best of three games

explanation.surface: Several golf professionals with short clubs play a best-of-three match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' is golf in the surface but prostitute in the definition; scrubber is British slang for a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubber is coarse British slang for a woman of loose morals, sometimes a prostitute.

clue.text: Musical piece — take care to retain old carbon copy

indicators.note: to retain means to hold inside, so the farewell word wraps round the others

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye, like take care
CC is the abbreviation for carbon copy, as in emails

explanation.surface: A keyboard piece must be handled carefully to keep an old duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ta is a British farewell, so 'take care' is a goodbye rather than an instruction; 'to retain' wraps it round old and carbon copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a showy keyboard composition, so a piece of music.

clue.text: Fool social worker to house first and second

indicators.note: to house means to hold within, so the two outer pieces enclose the ordinal

parts.note: an ass is a fool
an ant is a social insect and a worker
1ST, with the figure read as letter I, is first

explanation.surface: A foolish social worker houses people on a first-come, second-come basis.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker is a crossword staple for ANT, an insect living in colonies. 'second' is a noun: a helper, as at a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: A second at a duel or in boxing is the helper or aide in the corner.

clue.text: Award rest to break mechanical repetition

indicators.note: to break means to split open, so the resting word goes into the middle of the repetition word

parts.note: learning by rote is mechanical repetition
to set something down is to rest it

explanation.surface: Someone is given a break from monotonous drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like a noun but is a verb, to put down; 'to break' splits the rote-learning word to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon rosette is a prize badge given at shows, so an award.

clue.text: Swell man set up winning service, interrupted by news

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Swell man set up winning service, interrupted by news' parses as rev(HE) and ACE each interrupted by one N, 'news' read as N's (E(N)H + A(N)CE); the one indicator serves both insertions, which the grammar can express only with a shared indicator (refused) or a scattered rep() insertion, which crashes the checker's display.
annotationWithheld.clue: Swell man set up winning service, interrupted by news

clue.text: Book a rock group

definitions.meaning: the first book of the Bible
the English progressive rock band of Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins

explanation.definitionFit: The opening book of the Old Testament shares its name with a British prog-rock band.

clue.text: Chicken, one thus ready for eating?

definitions.meaning: a bird ready for the oven has had its innards removed

explanation.definitionFit: Cowardly people lack guts, courage; a dressed bird has had its insides taken out for cooking.

clue.text: It could provide cover for a skier

definitions.text: It could provide cover for a skier

parts.words: It could provide cover for a skier
parts.note: cover means a hat for the head, not insurance or shelter; a woolly one topped with a pompom suits the slopes

explanation.surface: Something might give insurance to someone on the ski slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' suggests insurance; it means headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted winter cap with a woolly pompom on top keeps a skier's head warm.

clue.text: French city, in report, twinned with Bristol?

indicators.note: in report means spoken, so the letters entered sound like another word

parts.note: Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol City, titty) for breasts, which come in pairs

explanation.surface: A French city is said to be twinned with an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristols is British rhyming slang for breasts, so one of a pair is a breast, which sounds like the city. The surface suggests town twinning.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval port at the tip of Brittany is a city in France.

clue.text: Composed, with chopped fish, fancy course

indicators.note: chopped means cut out, so the fish's letters are removed from the word composed
fancy means elaborate, inventive, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the cod is a common fish

explanation.surface: A calm diner with chopped fish orders an elaborate dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Take COD out of COMPOSED to leave MPOSE, then rearrange. 'course' looks culinary but is a racecourse: Epsom in Surrey hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey racecourse where the Derby is run is a famous track.

clue.text: Maybe typed under regular censorship? I think not

indicators.note: regular censorship means every other letter is cut out, keeping alternate letters of the words

explanation.surface: Something perhaps typed under routine censorship is denied.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'Maybe typed'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief, a scornful 'nonsense'.

clue.text: Butler's work-send back two presents after a slight mix-up

indicators.note: send back means turn round, so the letters are read in reverse
a slight mix-up means only a small rearrangement, here two letters trade places

parts.note: now and here are two words for the present, in time and place
now and here are two words for the present, in time and place

explanation.surface: A butler's job is to return two gifts after a little confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Butler's satire is the title. Reverse NOW HERE to get EREHWON, then the 'slight mix-up' swaps H and W.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1872 satirical utopian novel by Samuel Butler bears this title.

clue.text: Discharge from bottom of sea cow found by its head

indicators.note: from bottom of picks the final letter of the sea cow word to be moved
found by its head means placed at the front of the word

parts.note: the manatee is a sea cow

explanation.surface: Something is released from the seabed by a sea cow's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of MANATEE moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or issue, the verb sense of discharge.

clue.text: Quiet tot fed by vacuous half-wit

indicators.note: fed by means filled with, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to tot up is to sum, and a tot is a sum

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters of half-wit remain

explanation.surface: A silent toddler is fed by an empty-headed fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' empties HALF-WIT to HT; 'fed by' puts it in SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping silent or saying nothing, from Yiddish; 'keep schtum' means stay silent.

clue.text: For example, European put about note and short composition

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the put word goes round the example word

parts.note: to set is to put
say means for example
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A European writer, for example, sets down a note and a short essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the word for put round the word for for example; 'note' is the sol-fa syllable added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A little essay, with the diminutive suffix -ette.
